description: Money is just paper and metal. But we load it with meaning—fear, hope, shame, power, love and worth. Investigate where your money goes and test one money rule for seven days.

measurement.claimsBoundary: Behaviour Evidence Indicators describe source-specific learner evidence. They are not validated psychometric measures, diagnoses, forensic markers or proof of causation.

beiSchema.scoringRule: Record the selected workbook response from 1 to 10 without norming or classification.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: A single learner self-rating; it is not a validated measure of money capability.

beiSchema.construct: Self-reported frequency of workbook behaviours related to money
beiSchema.scoringRule: Retain all ten item responses from 1 to 5. A mean may be displayed only when every item is answered and must remain descriptive.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: The item set is not a validated scale and must not be used to diagnose or label a learner.

beiSchema.construct: Learner comparison of a prediction with the revealed story outcome
beiSchema.scoringRule: Record Yes as 1 and No as 0 for this workbook episode only.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: One story prediction is not a general calibration measure.

beiSchema.construct: Confidence in the learner-authored money equation
beiSchema.scoringRule: Record the selected workbook response from 1 to 10 without norming or classification.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: Confidence does not establish that the learner-authored equation is accurate.

beiSchema.construct: Self-reported areas affected by the selected money pattern
beiSchema.scoringRule: Retain each selected workbook area as selected or not selected; do not create a risk classification or threshold.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: This is not a clinical, safeguarding, actuarial or organisational risk assessment.

beiSchema.construct: Learner-recorded completion of the selected routine or rule
beiSchema.scoringRule: Count Done responses across seven days and report the observed count as x/7. Missing days remain missing and are not treated as zero.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: The record is learner-entered and does not by itself establish sustained adherence.

beiSchema.scoringRule: Record the selected workbook response from 1 to 10. A difference from BEI-01 may be shown as learner-reported change only.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: A pre/post self-rating difference is not proof that the Lab caused change.

beiSchema.construct: Confidence in the learner-authored money equation
beiSchema.scoringRule: Record the selected workbook response from 1 to 10. A difference from BEI-04 may be shown as learner-reported change only.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: A confidence difference is not evidence that the equation became more accurate.

beiSchema.scoringRule: Record completion and preserve the private learner-authored text; do not score sentiment or identity.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: Completion does not demonstrate an identity shift.

beiSchema.construct: Learner synthesis of the Money Lab evidence
beiSchema.scoringRule: Record completion and preserve the private learner-authored summary; no automated profile is generated.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: The summary is a learner reflection, not a behavioural classification.

### BEI-01: Money Consciousness Index (Pre)

"On a scale of 1–10, how conscious are you of where your money actually goes? 1 = I have no idea. 10 = I know exactly where every rand goes."

### INVESTIGATION 1: THE HOOK

MISSION: Meet someone whose money lesson changed everything.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ A prediction about what you would do

TIME: 5 minutes

DIFFICULTY:          Observe

### 📖 Read

Episode 1: The Girl Who Counted Coins

Meet Myah.

Myah is fifteen. She lives with her mother in a small house near the taxi rank. Her mother counts coins every morning—pension money, carefully rationed.

Myah watches.

She has always watched. She sees the vendors at the taxi rank. She sees the money flowing between everyone. She sees her mother counting coins. She writes in her small notebook.

She has never said what she notices out loud.

She has R10 in her pocket. Her mother gave it to her for vegetables at the spaza shop. The vegetables cost R8. She has R2 left.

She stands at the counter. She could buy something. A cold drink. A snack. Something small. Something that feels like she chose it.

She does not buy anything.

She puts the R2 in her pocket. She walks home. She does not know why she did not spend it. She just felt like she should save it. Like she should hold onto it.

That night, her mother counts coins again. Myah watches. Her mother says: "We have enough for the week. Just enough."

Myah writes in her notebook: "I am someone who notices."

She has been writing that for months.

She still does not know what she is becoming.

But she is starting to see patterns. Scarcity. Fear. The way money moves through her life without her ever touching it, except for the change her mother gives her.

She is fifteen. She has R2 saved. She has no plan. She has no savings. She has no idea what she is becoming.

But she is watching.

And something is shifting.

### INVESTIGATION 3: THE REVELATION

MISSION: Discover the hidden structure of your money decisions.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ Understanding of money triggers
● ☐ Prediction calibration check

TIME: 3 minutes

DIFFICULTY:          Analyse

### 📖 Read

Episode 2: What Myah Didn't See

Myah saved R2. She did not spend it. She did not even want anything. She just wanted to hold onto something.

She has been watching her mother count coins for years. She has been seeing the scarcity. She has been writing in her notebook.

But here is what nobody told her: money is the most emotional object in the world. It is just paper and metal. But we have loaded it with meaning—fear, hope, shame, power, love, worth.

We do not spend money rationally. We spend it emotionally. Then we justify it rationally.

Myah's mother does not spend money. She rations it. She survives. She does not plan. She does not invest. She just gets through.

Myah is starting to see the pattern. But she is fifteen. She has R2 saved. She has no plan. She has no idea what she is building.

The next day, she walks past the spaza shop. She sees Sipho—the boy who fixed the radio— standing outside with a packet of screws. He looks at her.

"You're the girl with the notebook," he says.

She nods.

"What do you write in there?"

She does not know what to say. She looks at him. "I write about what I see."

He nods. "I'm building something," he says. "I don't know what yet. But I'm building it."

She watches him walk away.

She opens her notebook. She writes: "I want to understand money. Where it comes from. Where it goes. How it works. I want to help my mother instead of just taking from her."

She closes the notebook.

She is fifteen. She has R2 saved. She has no plan. She has no idea what she is becoming.

But she just wrote it down.

And something shifted.
